title: The Munich Microfluidics Toolkit: Design Automation and Simulation Tools for Microfluidic Devices
problem: Microfluidic device design lacks comprehensive open-source design automation and multi-level simulation tools.
motivation: Integrated design automation toolkit accelerates microfluidic device development and lowers barriers to entry for researchers.
method: The toolkit takes specifications for a microfluidic device and automatically generates designs from them. It validates these designs through simulations at multiple levels—first testing individual components, then testing the complete system. As an open-source tool supporting diverse microfluidic design approaches, it can be used and adapted for different research needs.
key_novelty: This toolkit brings together automatic design generation and multi-level simulation validation for microfluidic devices in a single open-source package.
limitations: Performance benchmarks against manual design processes not provided; scalability to large-scale microfluidic systems unclear.
primary_theme: Design automation toolkit for microfluidic devices
